evidence_summary: METHOD: Discovery via WebSearch on template title formulas (YouTube.com itself was proxy-blocked; search.list quota exhausted as instructed); every number verified via YouTube Data API v3 channels.list / playlistItems.list / videos.list. ~35 videos and 20+ channels checked; cohort of 6 channels created within the last 12 months on the exact format, plus the exemplar and 8 comparators/pivots. KEY FINDINGS: (1) The exemplar claim checks out — Edwards Economics' first upload was 2025-03-26 and the channel now has 358k subs / 12.3M views on 90 videos — but his per-video performance has fallen ~4x (upload-quarter median 215k for 2025Q2 vs 56k for 2026Q2 and ~20-29k for early Q3 uploads). (2) The algorithm still cold-tests new channels: Pricing Market (created Dec 2025) put up a 57k-view video in its first active month; The Unfolded States opened at 27-41k median views/month; Economic Cycles hit 30k in month one. So distribution is not CLOSED. (3) But conversion is zero in the observed cohort: all five true cold-starts are failing, stalled, pivoted, or abandoned; the only thriving sub-12-month channel is a cross-promoted spinoff of a 241k-sub incumbent. The Unfolded States is the cleanest natural experiment — 197 daily uploads, exact template, and its monthly upload-cohort median views declined every single month from 37.3k (Nov 2025) to 1.8k (Jul 2026). (4) The niche's browse shelf is being captured by established pivots (Zac Rios 482k views/video, Yak Motley, A Homestead Journey, Frugal Fit Mom, even Brookings), which raises the bar for cold-starts far above what Edwards faced in March 2025. (5) Macro did NOT improve — headline inflation reaccelerated to ~4.2% by mid-2026 (Hormuz oil shock) and Michigan sentiment is ~20% below a year ago — so the observed view decay is supply-saturation-driven, not demand-driven; a future macro improvement is an additional untested downside. (6) Monetization: no direct creator reports of yellow-icon limited ads on layoff/affordability topics were found (honest null); the documented and larger risk is YouTube's July 15, 2025 'inauthentic content' YPP policy explicitly targeting mass-produced, template-based content — a channel-level demonetization risk aimed at precisely this production style. SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS CAVEAT ON MY OWN METHOD: web search surfaces videos that rank, so my cohort over-represents channels that got at least one distribution spike; channels created in H1 2026 that never escaped double-digit views are essentially invisible to this method (I found zero H1 2026-created channels at all — that absence is a discovery artifact, not evidence none exist), and the failures I did find (97-view, 30-view uploads) surfaced only incidentally. The true failure rate of the entering cohort is therefore strictly HIGHER than what this table shows.

answers.question: (1) Enumerate channels launched on this template in the last 6-9 months and measure whether sub-10k-sub entrants uploading NOW still get browse distribution
answers.answer: Five true cold-starts found in the Oct-Dec 2025 launch window (The Unfolded States 2025-08, Economic Cycles 2025-10, Pricing Market 2025-12, The New Exodus 2025-12, Stack Loaded 2025-12) plus one warm-start spinoff (A Homestead Journey Clips 2025-11). Sub-10k entrants uploading NOW: The Unfolded States (9.9k subs) gets 1.8-3.7k views on July 2026 uploads — real but small and declining browse distribution; Economic Cycles (3.2k subs) gets 100-1,300; Pricing Market fell to 30-50 views and quit in May; New Exodus and Stack Loaded pivoted away then stopped. The algorithm demonstrably still gives NEW channels an initial test (57k, 30k, 41k first-month maxima as late as Feb 2026), so a well-executed August 2026 launch would likely get impressions — but no cold-start in the cohort converted the test into compounding distribution, and per-video medians decayed monotonically for every one of them. 0/5 cold-starts thriving; 1/1 warm-start thriving. Verified via channels.list + playlistItems.list + videos.list on each channelId listed in the cohort table.

answers.question: (2) Do layoff/affordability topics trigger limited-ads (yellow icons / RPM reports)?
answers.answer: No direct creator reports of yellow icons specifically on layoff/affordability/cost-of-living videos were found after multiple targeted searches (Reddit fetch was also blocked in this environment) — treat as an honest null, not an all-clear. Indirect evidence cuts both ways: finance/economics is consistently reported as the highest-RPM niche ($10-25+ per outlierkit.com and fluxnote.io, low-medium reliability), and Edwards-style channels keep producing layoff titles at high volume (his single best recent video, 194k views, is 'Mass Layoffs Are Coming for White Collar Jobs in 2026'), which sustained-volume behavior is inconsistent with severe limited-ads pain. The BIGGER documented monetization risk is format-level, not topic-level: YouTube's July 15, 2025 YPP 'inauthentic content' policy (support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392) explicitly targets template-based, mass-produced content 'with little to no variation across videos' and applies channel-wide — this cohort's exact production style. 2026 trade-blog reports of enforcement waves removing $7k-30k/month template channels exist but are low-reliability SEO content (sweettntmagazine.com, sueio.com); the policy itself is official and high-reliability.

answers.question: (3) Does demand survive macro improvement — view decay on 2025-vintage doom videos vs evergreen framings?
answers.answer: The premise is partly moot: macro has NOT improved — headline inflation reaccelerated to ~4.2% by mid-2026 after the Strait of Hormuz shock, and Michigan consumer sentiment is ~20% below a year ago (sca.isr.umich.edu, CNN, Deloitte). Yet per-video views are decaying anyway: Edwards' upload-quarter median fell 215k→56k (2025Q2→2026Q2) and every new-cohort channel shows monotonic monthly decline. Conclusion: the decay is SUPPLY saturation (incumbent pivots + copycat flood), not demand loss — meaning a macro improvement is an additional, still-untested downside on top of an already-decaying opportunity. Note the API only exposes cumulative views, so true time-decay on 2025-vintage videos is not directly measurable; upload-cohort medians are the proxy used. On framings: within Edwards' last 10 uploads, evergreen-structural topics beat vibe-doom — housing lock-in (s2Cuu9SpbgA) 40.9k and retiring-broke math (H8r4cPbPTJ0) 53.9k vs Gen Z-too-broke 12.9k and grocery-doom 11.3k — and his layoffs video (194k) shows event-driven labor topics still spike hardest. Weak but consistent evidence that structural/evergreen framings (housing lock-in, retirement math) hold distribution better than generic 'everything is terrible' titles.
